findings.message: The diff removes the `.card.flush tbody tr` region from the 001 releases visual check because the rows now follow 125. No region was added that compares the new rows with the `125-release-pages` mock section (.specclaw/mock/index.html:4081). As a result, nothing compares the new list rows with any mock. Fix: add a SECTIONS entry for 125-release-pages that covers the list rows, filters and release page cards. If a gap is intended, record it in the known-gaps list with its reason.
findings.scenario: The release table's row layout drifts from the 125 mock (for example, the Category column is dropped) → the visual spec still passes.

findings.message: `namesFor` turns actor strings into names from auth.user and auth.service_principal. `server/proposal-detail.ts:129` already does the same lookup with its own query. The two copies can drift, for example in how they treat an `sp:` id or an inactive user. Fix: have proposal-detail use `namesFor`, so the 'who' on the proposal page and on the release page come from one rule.

The server renders the time with a 'UTC' label. After hydration, the ref callback overwrites `textContent` with the local time, which has no time zone label. The reader can then no longer tell which zone the time is in. Writing to the DOM directly also bypasses React, so if the `at` prop changes, the time React renders and the time on screen can disagree. Fix: include the zone in the local format (for example `timeZoneName: "short"`) and set the text from state in an effect, not by writing to the DOM.
findings.scenario: A deployment row shows '12 Dec 2026, 20:05 UTC' from the server. After hydration it shows '13 Dec 2026, 01:35' with no zone, next to a release day that is in the project's zone.

findings.message: The release page works out `completedDay` (and the voided day) at read time, using the project's legal-entity zone as it is now. `completion` (On time/Late) was decided once, at completion time, with the zone that applied then (completeBy → releaseDay(zoneOf…)). Since 126, Completed is final, so `completion` never changes, but the day shown beside it moves whenever the project's legal entity or the entity's zone changes. The page can then show a completion day after the target next to "On time", or the reverse. That is the same day-vs-verdict split the earlier B4 lesson flagged, now caused by a config change rather than a UTC/zone mismatch. Fix: when completeBy runs, store the completion day (a `completed_day` date column, or the zone used) and have getRelease/completedLine read that stored day. Add a test that changes the entity zone after completion.
findings.scenario: Project RTK has no legal entity, so it uses UTC. The release targets 2026-12-11 and its UAT deployment is at 2026-12-11T23:00Z, so it completes on_time. An Admin then links RTK to an entity in Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14). The release page now reads "Completed on 12 Dec 2026 · On time", one day after the 11 Dec target.

findings.message: `Loaded` catches every error from `load` and shows "Couldn't load … Try again". Only Next control-flow errors get rethrown. A ForbiddenError (a viewer without delivery:read) or a not-found error therefore looks like a temporary read failure, and retrying will never help. Rethrow ForbiddenError, or give it its own message, so a permission refusal isn't shown as a transient fault.
findings.scenario: A Finance-only viewer without delivery:read opens /delivery/releases/CON/v2.4.0. getRelease throws ForbiddenError, and the page says "Couldn't load this release." with a Try again link instead of saying they can't see it.

findings.message: The edit card writes its own completed-release refusal (`${projectKey} ${version} is completed; it can't change`) instead of reusing `notCompleted` from release-tracking.ts, which update_release uses. Today the two strings match, but they are two copies of one rule. Export the message (as was done with notTrackedYet) and use it in both places.

The Release tracking (123) paragraph still ends "The daily status check and the screens are later phases." This change ships both: the hourly check (126) and the release pages (125). Remove or update that sentence. It also calls the check daily, but it runs hourly.
